title: Contextualization & latency tradeoffs — reading notes
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad while skimming a mix of papers, blog posts, and recent internal threads. Goal is to pull concrete tradeoffs we can test in the next sprint (email summarization use-case + cheap hosting options).

1) Paper: "Fast Prefix Caching for Long-Context Generation" (preprint, Apr 2026) — notes
- Core idea: maintain prefix fingerprints at multiple granularities and do incremental KV cache retrieval instead of full-context attention for repeated patterns (e.g., email headers, quoted threads).
- Why relevant: our email summarization workload has very high prefix repetition (greetings, quoted chains); could cut token work by ~1.8–3x for typical threads.
- Assumptions/limits: works best when repetition ratio > 25% and when model supports partial attention slices; degrades with frequent edits.
- Implementation thoughts for Redwood: add a caching tier that stores canonicalized prefix vectors keyed by fingerprint + schema (e.g., header-only, body-only). Integrate with existing KV cache retrieval hooks.
- Quick experiment idea: instrument 1k email threads from internal dataset; compute repetition ratio; run simulated token-cost model with and without prefix-caching using our existing runtime traces.
- Open question: how to handle alignment drift when user edits middle of thread — need invalidation policy; cheap heuristic: ttl + edit-detection by diffing last N tokens.

2) Blog post: "Quantized decoding on commodity GPUs" (engineering blog, May 2026) — takeaway
- Observed throughput improvements when decoding with 4-bit quant and mixed precision kernels; however, tail-latency increases for short-utterance requests due to kernel launch overhead.
- For hosted API: batching helps, but for low-latency interactive features (email compose inline suggestions) batching harm UX.
- Actionable: evaluate 4-bit quantized variants targeted at dedicated pools with short-burst warmup and microbatching (batch size 1–4) optimizations. Measure 95th/99th percentiles separately.

3) Conference notes: Systems@Scale workshop — "Graceful degradation by fallbacks" panel
- Practical patterns: maintain a small, fast rehearsal model (tiny distilled 100M–300M) to return partial responses within strict SLO, while downstream async job builds full response.
- For email UX: can we serve first-pass subject-line or 1–2 sentence summary from rehearsal model under 150ms, then stream fuller summary? Might improve perceived latency even if complete response arrives later.
- UX constraint: must avoid mismatch / factual contradictions between rehearsal and final model. Potential mitigation: rehearsal outputs only structural suggestions (e.g., bullet skeletons), not factual claims.

4) Internal thread summary (Slack #kv-cache) — quick notes
- Arjun: eviction policy experiments showed LRU+frequency hybrid reduces thrash for conversational workloads.
- Kira: pruning by topic cluster (cheap hashing over semantic embeddings) reduces unnecessary cache volume for multi-conversant threads.
- My thought: combine fingerprint-based prefix caching with cluster-aware eviction — store cluster id with cached prefixes so similar threads share entries.

Concrete experiments to run (next 2 weeks)
- Exp A (analysis): run replication analysis on 5k real threads -> compute prefix repetition distribution, percent of tokens saved if prefix-cached. Metric: token-saved-per-request, plus reconstruction error when prefixes trimmed. Data owner: @Kira.
- Exp B (runtime sim): use recorded traces from hosted API for short-utterance email suggestions. Simulate 4-bit quant kernels + microbatch size 1 to measure P50/P95/P99 latency and token cost. Metric: cost-per-1000-requests, P95 latency under 250ms. Owner: @Arjun.
- Exp C (fallback sketch): prototype a rehearsal-model workflow in a simple lambda: rehearsal returns bullet outline (max 40 tokens) in <150ms; full model streams final text. Evaluate UX mismatch with small user panel. Metric: user perceived latency and coherence delta. Owner: me (Eden).

Prompts / quick examples to test
- Prompt for rehearsal outline (conservative): "Read the following email thread and produce a 3-bullet outline capturing topics and action items. Do not invent facts."
- Full generation prompt (final): include system note: "Use outline provided by rehearsal. If outline is incomplete, retrieve from conversation history before adding facts."

Risks / unknowns
- Cache invalidation complexity when users edit earlier messages — could risk stale summaries. Need conservative ttl or edit-triggered invalidation.
- Quality regression from quantized model that our eval harness might not catch; need to pair with lightweight automated evals (ROUGE + instruction-following checks).
- Operational: storing lots of prefix fingerprints increases metadata; consider sharding keys and TTL to control storage.

Links & references (quick)
- https://paper.org/long-context-email-2026 (prefix caching preprint)
- https://blog.engineering/quant-decode-may-2026 (quantized decoding notes)
- GH#redwood/kv-cache-experiments/42 (internal PR with LRU+freq tests)
- JIRA-ENG-1287 (proposal: rehearsal-model rollout for low-latency features)

Notes-to-self (short)
- Talk to @Kira about dataset access and quick sampling script.
- Spin up microbench harness that uses recorded traces; don't try to re-run on prod GPUs. Use devpool GPUs with same kernel builds.
- Add evaluation checklist: automatic mismatch detector between rehearsal and final response (simple overlap + hallucination flag).

Unresolved questions (for discussion)
- Acceptable coherence gap between rehearsal and final? propose threshold: <15% divergence in named entities and core facts. Need metricization.
- Is prefix-caching worth complexity for use-cases where repetition ratio ~10–20%? need to decide a hard cutoff.

End of notes.

-- Eden
